2.text: Every wind is blowing upon it; every wave is washing over it. I am safe.”

3.text: It is good also to swallow a small stone. Then, when the keˊlᴇ comes, he

4.text: cannot find the man among the pebbles on the shore.

5.text: Told by Aiñanwaˊt, a Reindeer Chukchee man, in the Kolyma Country, 1895.

6.text: (e) If I am afraid of keˊlet, when travelling alone in the night-time, I

7.text: take the throat of a reˊkkeñ¹ for my road. He has a long neck. Travelling

8.text: inside of it, the other keˊlet would not be able to find me.

9.text: Told by Qoˊtêrg̣ɪn (man) in the village of Mɪˊs˙qᴀn, 1900.

10.text: 6. INCANTATION USED TO PROTECT THE HERD FROM THE HOOF-DISEASE.

11.text: I ask from the Master of the Pebbly River a big iron box. I put into it

12.text: my herd, and then turn the key. How can he (that is, the keˊlᴇ) enter there?

13.text: 7. INCANTATION AGAINST ATTACK by WOLVES, TO BE USED BY A HERDSMAN.

14.text: To protect my herd from wolves, I surround it with a long line suspended

15.text: in the air. Upon this line I hang a number of clothes, which swing in all

16.text: directions, and frighten the wolves. Thus they cannot approach the herd.

17.text: Nos. 6 & 7 told by Scratching-Woman at Mariinsky Post, 1900.

19.text: (a) I went out into the open air. At some distance from the house

20.text: there are hummocks, — two hummocks covered with grass. One of them

21.text: is the nearer, although it is no great distance away. I suppose that I have

22.text: travelled as far as the region beyond the skies. Coming quite close to the

23.text: nearer hummock, I cry out, “Halloo!” I say it to myself, but it is as if the

24.text: hummock called to me. Then I answer, “No, it is I!” — “How wonderful!

25.text: Where from?” — “No, I come from the people below!” — “How wonderful!

26.text: For what have you come? You have come from a very long distance.” It

27.text: is a little old woman who talks to me, — a Woman of the First Creation,

28.text: Kuˊčä-ñeˊut by name, who is sitting in the inner room of her house. The

29.text: other hummock is her neighbor, the chief inhabitant of the place. She is a

30.text: woman of many incantations: her name is Raˊučha-ñaˊut.² “Well, let us hear
30.note: "čh" gets reduced to "č" a lot presumably because of its pronunciation

31.text: what the other woman will say, — Raˊučha-ñaˊut, the possessor of the incan-

32.text: tations. Go to her!” I start as if about to go farther on to the chief house.

33.text: Again a conversation, as the first time. “Halloo!” — “Who is there?” —

34.text: “No, it is I!” — “How wonderful! Where from?” — “I belong to the people

37.text: meaning of the first half of each name was unknown to the speaker.
